findings.source_basis: sources/prd-original.txt:1 (hash 347413d5…219d) states: all three APIs getHostUserInfo, getHostUserInfoAll and getUserInfoAll must return systemLanguages ["de-DE", "en-GB"] when passed exactly the ordered input ["de-DE", "en-GB"]. spec/requirements.json R-1 (confirmed) has the same acceptance criterion.
findings.required_scope: Three targets: getHostUserInfo, getHostUserInfoAll and getUserInfoAll in convert.py. Precondition: each is given exactly the ordered input ["de-DE", "en-GB"]. Outcome: each one's systemLanguages is exactly ["de-DE", "en-GB"], with the same order and length. Build: b9360076c9789ba4123ac5c6d81dc2eed0d54ddd.
findings.observed_scope: Runtime execution at b9360076: test_language.py:5-6 calls only getHostUserInfo, and only with ["de-DE", "fr-FR"]. That is a nearby pair, not the specified one. quality-report.json shows 1 test ran and passed. No run touched getHostUserInfoAll or getUserInfoAll, and no run used ["de-DE", "en-GB"]. The recorded manual evidence admits this: 'Only getHostUserInfo on [de-DE,fr-FR] executed; other APIs and exact pair not run'. The 'passed' status was asserted, not observed. Inference from reading code, not execution: convert.py:1-2 and 4-5 are pure deterministic functions returning list(device_languages), so getHostUserInfo and getHostUserInfoAll would return ["de-DE", "en-GB"] for that input. This inference is sound because there is no state, I/O or branching. convert.py:7-8 getUserInfoAll returns list(device_languages[:1]), which deterministically gives ["de-DE"].

findings.counterexample_check: Concrete case: getUserInfoAll(["de-DE", "en-GB"]). From the code, the result is {"systemLanguages": ["de-DE"]}. This violates the claim because en-GB is dropped. The current evidence allows this case and does not catch it, since no test calls getUserInfoAll. For getHostUserInfoAll, the claim also has no runtime evidence; only code inference supports it. The 'passed' result is therefore unsupported for full scope, and the claim is actually false for one of the three APIs.

findings.source_basis: impact.json behaviors B-1 (kind change, basis R-1): 'All three API entry points preserve the exact specified system language pair'. It traces back to sources/prd-original.txt:1.
findings.required_scope: All three entry points, getHostUserInfo, getHostUserInfoAll and getUserInfoAll, must preserve the exact specified pair ["de-DE", "en-GB"] in order and in full in systemLanguages. Build: b9360076c9789ba4123ac5c6d81dc2eed0d54ddd. Shared state (state.py) is in the inspected paths.
findings.observed_scope: Runtime execution at b9360076: only getHostUserInfo was run, with the non-specified pair ["de-DE", "fr-FR"] (test_language.py:6). The other two entry points were never executed, and neither was the specified pair. The manual evidence string confirms this. Inference: state.py contains only the literal 'shared' and nothing in convert.py imports it, so it has no effect on these functions. Code reading shows getHostUserInfo and getHostUserInfoAll preserve their input. getUserInfoAll truncates to the first element (convert.py:8) and therefore does not preserve the pair.

findings.counterexample_check: Concrete case: getUserInfoAll(["de-DE", "en-GB"]) yields ["de-DE"], so the entry point does not preserve the pair. This violates B-1. The recorded evidence, a one-API, nearby-pair run, allows this defect and cannot detect it. A test that passes for one interface on [de-DE, fr-FR] cannot stand for three interfaces on [de-DE, en-GB].
